```{r Load Packages}
# Load packages
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(plotly)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(peRReo)
library(kableExtra)
library(maps)
library(PNWColors)
```

## Introduction

This analysis uses monitoring data from Palikea Gulch, related to an endemic mint restoration project. The two reusable functions are as follows:

1.  `summarise_mint()` calculates summary stats for any numeric measurement grouped by treatment
2.  `plot_mint()` creates a consistent plot for any numeric measurements and selected variables

```{r Setup Data}

# Read the Palikea Data
palikea_raw <- read_csv(
  here("Week_08", "Data", "PalikeaRaw.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Clean up column names
paliklean <- palikea_raw |>
  rename(
    survival = `Alive/Dead`,
    height_cm = `Height (cm)`,
    leaf_count = LeafCount
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across( # Make below columns factors
      c(
        Genotype,
        Inocula,
        Frequency,
        Site,
        survival),
      as.factor),

    Timepoint = as.integer(Timepoint), # Mutate Timepoint to integers

    genotype_inocula = interaction( # Add column that combines Genotype and Inocula
      Genotype,
      Inocula,
      sep = " + "),

    full_treatment = interaction( # Add column that combines Genotype, Inocula, and Frequency 
      Genotype,
      Inocula,
      Frequency,
      sep = " + "))

head(paliklean)
```

- Clean dataset contains:
  - `r nrow(paliklean)` observations
  - `r n_distinct(paliklean$PlantID)` individual plants

## Function 1: Summary

- Remember the 4 elements to make a formula:

1.  `data`: the dataset
2.  `response`: what I'm measuring
3.  `group`: grouping parameter
4.  `survivors`: whether to include only the remaining plants

```{r Summary Function}
summarize_mint <- function(
    data,
    group,
    response = NULL, # Means that measurement assumes no response unless one provided
    survivors = TRUE, # Assumption is that we only want to analyze the surviving plants
    survival_progression = FALSE) {
  
  if (survival_progression == TRUE) { # Use this if you want to see progress of survival between outplanting until the specific monitoring day / timepoint
    summary_data <- data |>
      group_by(
        {{group}},
        Timepoint) |>
  summarise(
    total_plants = n_distinct(PlantID),
      living_plants = n_distinct(PlantID[survival == "Alive"]),
      dead_plants = n_distinct(PlantID[survival == "Dead"]),
      survival_ratio = living_plants / total_plants,
      survival_perc = survival_ratio * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
  } else {
    if (survivors == TRUE) { 
      data <- data |>
        filter(
          Timepoint == 2, # Timepoint 2 is used since that represent the most up to date monitoring data
          survival == "Alive"
        )
  }
  
  summary_data <- data |>
    group_by({{group}}) |>
    summarise(
      n = sum(!is.na({{response}})),
      mean = mean({{response}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd = sd({{response}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      se = sd / sqrt(n),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  }
  
  return(summary_data)
}
```

### Example 1: Height by Inoculum and Genotype

- Calculates the plant-height statistics for each inoculum treatment
  - Because `survivors` defaults to `TRUE` only plants recorded as alive are included unless otherwise indicated

```{r Height by Treatment Table}
#| warning: FALSE
#| label: tbl-height-by-treatment
#| tbl-cap: "Height of Surviving Palikea Mints by Treatment"

summarize_mint(
  data = paliklean,
  group = full_treatment,
  response = height_cm,
  survival_progression = FALSE) |>
  mutate(across(
    c(mean, sd, se),
    ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Full Treatment",
      "n",
      "Mean (cm)",
      "SD",
      "SE")) |>
  kable_classic()
```

### Example 2: Leaf Counts by Treatment

- Same function, different biological question
- What I'm changing:
  - `response` to `Leaf Count`

```{r Leaf Counts by Treatment Table}
#| warning: FALSE
#| label: tbl-leaf-by-treatment
#| tbl-cap: "Leaf Count Among Surviving Mints"

summarize_mint(
  data = paliklean,
  group = full_treatment,
  response = leaf_count) |>
  mutate(across(
    c(mean, sd, se),
    ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Full Treatment",
      "n",
      "Mean Leaf Count",
      "SD",
      "SE")) |>
  kable_classic()

```

#### Combine Tables to Have Full Summary

- The `tbl-mint-summary` combines `tbl-height-by-treatment` and `tbl-leaves-by-treatment`
  - The last column describes what the measurement is

```{r Combining Tables}
#| warning: FALSE
#| label: tbl-mint-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary Table of Surviving Palikea Mints"

mint_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarize_mint(
    data = paliklean,
    group = genotype_inocula,
    response = height_cm) |>
    mutate(measurement = "Height (cm)"), # Make column before binding
  
  summarize_mint(
    data = paliklean,
    group = genotype_inocula,
    response = leaf_count) |>
    mutate(measurement = "Leaf Count") # See above, need to make column for summary table
  ) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Genotype + Inocula",
      "n",
      "Mean",
      "SD",
      "SE",
      "Measurement")) |> # Need this column so that reader knows what the associated data is attached to
  kable_classic()

mint_summary
```

### Example 3: Survival Progression Table

- Here, we set `survival_progression = TRUE`, so it does not truncate the data frame to only the survivors, allowing summary of surviving plants through each monitoring point
  - `arrange(Timepoint)` arranges each column by Outplant (0), Quarter 1 (1), and Quarter 2 (2)

```{r Survial Progression Table}
#| warning: FALSE
#| label: tbl-survival-progression-genotype
#| tbl-cap: "Survival Progression of Palikea Mints"

summarize_mint(
  data = paliklean,
  group = genotype_inocula,
  survival_progression = TRUE) |>
  arrange(Timepoint) |>
  kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Genotype + Inocula",
      "Timepoint",
      "Outplant Total",
      "Living Plants",
      "Dead Plants",
      "Survival Ratio",
      "Survival Percentage"
    )
  ) |>
  kable_classic()
  
```

## Function 2: Minty Plot

Plotting function uses the `summarize_mint()`to calculate means and standard errors.

- User can change:
  - Response variable
  - Grouping variable
  - Labels, titles, etc.
  - Colors
  - Raw observations
  - Whether dead plants are excluded

```{r Defining Plot Function}

minty_plot <- function(
    data,
    group,
    response = NULL, # Again, assumes no response to but can change this parameter by giving response a value
    survivors = TRUE, # Assumption to assume analysis of surviving plants
    survival_progression = FALSE, # See above, only TRUE if we want to look at survival progression
    show_points = TRUE) {
  
  number_colors <- data |> # This is so that the colors are assigned according to the number of distinct grouping variables
    distinct({{group}}) |>
    nrow()
  
  pal <- pnw_palette( # PNW palette
    "Starfish",
    number_colors)
  
  
  ## BRANCH 1: SURVIVAL OVER TIME
  if(survival_progression == TRUE) {
    plot_summary <- summarize_mint(
      data = data,
      group = {{group}},
      survival_progression = TRUE)
  
  pali_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_summary,
  aes(
    x = Timepoint,
    y = survival_perc,
    color = {{ group }},
    group = {{ group }})) + # `group` in aes keeps one line per treatment
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(
      unique(plot_summary$Timepoint))) + 
  scale_y_continuous( # survival_perc is already 0-100 scale, so scale = 1 stops the label_percent() from multiplying by 100 again
    limits = c(0, 100),
    labels = scales::label_percent(
      scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Timepoint",
    y = "Survival (%)",
    color = "Treatment") +
  theme_gray()
      
  } else {
  
  ## BRANCH 2: GROUP MEANS OF A RESPONSE
    plot_summary <- summarize_mint(
      data = data,
      group = {{ group }},
      response = {{ response }},
      survivors = survivors,
      survival_progression = FALSE)
    
    plot_data <- data 
    
    if(survivors == TRUE) { # Match raw points to the data frame used for the summary 
      plot_data <- plot_data |>
        filter(
          Timepoint == 2,
          survival == "Alive")
    }
    pali_plot <- ggplot( # Plot uses plot_summary for bars, points uses the raw plot_data for points
      plot_summary,
      aes(
        x = {{group}},
        y = mean,
        fill = {{group}})) +
      geom_col(
        width = 0.7,
        alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_errorbar(
        aes(
          ymin = mean - se,
          ymax = mean + se),
        width = 0.15,
        linewidth = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = pal) +
      labs(
        x = "Treatment",
        y = "Mean",
        fill = "Treatment") +
      theme_gray()
    
    if(show_points == TRUE) { # Here I overlay the points
      pali_plot <- pali_plot +
        geom_jitter(
          data = plot_data,
          aes(
            x = {{ group }},
            y = {{ response }}),
          inherit.aes = FALSE, # Required because this layers reads raw data with different columns that those in plot_summary
          width = 0.1,
          height = 0,
          alpha = 0.5,
          size = 1.5)
    }
    }
  return(pali_plot) 
}
          
```

### Example 4: Height by Genotype

- Here, we define:
  - `response = height_cm`
  - `group = Genotype`
  - `survivors = TRUE`
  - `show_points = TRUE`

```{r Height of Survivors by Genotype Plot}
#| label: fig-height-genotype

minty_plot(
  data = paliklean,
  response = height_cm,
  group = Genotype,
  survivors = TRUE,
  show_points = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Height of Surviving Mints by Genotype",
    y = "Plant Height (cm)",
    x = "Genotype"
  )

```

### Example 5: Leaf Count by Genotype

- Here, we define:
  - `response = leaf_count`
  - `group = Genotype`
  - `survivors = TRUE`
  - `show_points = TRUE`

```{r Leaf Count by Genotype Plot}
#| label: fig-leaf-genotype

minty_plot(

  group = Genotype,
  survivors = TRUE,
  show_points = TRUE) +
```

### Example 6: Height of Survivors, Genotype + Treatment

- Here, we define:
  - `response = height_cm`
  - `group = genotype_inocula`, which is the interaction we defined in data setup, added associated column
  - `survivors = TRUE`
  - `show_points = TRUE`

```{r Height of Survivors of Gen ~ Treatment}
#| label: fig-height-gen-inocula

height_plot <- minty_plot(
  data = paliklean,
  response = height_cm,
  group = genotype_inocula,
  survivors = TRUE,
  show_points = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Height of Surviving Mints by Genotype + Treatment",
    y = "Plant Height (cm)",
    x = "Genotype + Inocula"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15,
                              face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45,
                               vjust = 0.6,
                               size = 6),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "grey87")
  )

height_plot
```
